Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the SOW. Happy to help. Short answers up front, and I can follow with a compact proposal once we understand a couple of volume points: 

- Billing model: we bill embeddings per-vector for the hosted API. For text inputs we also publish a mapping guidance (avg tokens -> vector) so you can estimate cost from token usage; for initial quoting we treat text->vector as 1 vector per call unless you batch multi-chunk mappings.
- Supported models/dims: RED-embed-512, RED-embed-1024, RED-embed-2048 (higher-dim previews), and a selection of vetted open models (OpenEmbed-768, OpenEmbed-1024). Production support and latency SLAs vary by model; we can call out the recommended ones for low-latency search.
- Higher-dim pricing: standard approach is a dimension multiplier. 1024 is ~1.6x the 512 base, 2048 ~1.75–2.0x depending on memory profile.
- Volume tiers: baseline (pay-as-you-go), 3 volume bands for committed discounts (250k, 1M, 5M vectors / mo). Typical uplift for enterprise commits: 15–30% off list depending on term and commit.
- Pilots: we can offer a 30-day pilot (up to 1M vectors) or a short-term credit against a first-month commit for qualified pilots.

I attached our current public ratecard (redwood_embed_ratecard_may2027.pdf). Can you confirm an expected monthly vector volume (ballpark) and which dimension you plan to standardize on? Once we have that we can send a tailored quote and an example price schedule mapped to your SOW.

If helpful I can also set a 30-minute call with our pricing lead and Dev to walk the economics and integration considerations.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

Eve / Marissa — quick technical notes for the proposal: 

1) Model support: RED-embed-512 (default), RED-embed-1024 (recommended for semantic re-ranking), and RED-embed-2048 (for high-fidelity semantic signal). We also support OpenEmbed-768/1024 variants but they are best-effort for SLA.

2) Pricing mapping: our runtime stores per-vector cost. Mapping text -> vector depends on chunking strategy; simplest estimate is 1 vector per document snippet or per request. For quoting purposes we use a conservative mapping of 1.2 vectors per average text query to account for chunking.

3) Dimension multiplier: use 512 as baseline. 1024 = x1.6 baseline. 2048 = x1.9 baseline in our quote (covers memory and I/O). Avoid quoting 2.0 unless legal permits — 1.9 is defensible.

4) Latency caveats: 2048 dims increase memory pressure and can bump p95 by ~30–60ms on small GPU pools. If they need <100ms p95 we should recommend 512/1024 and use caching.

5) Pilot: technical pilot can be done within hosted environment; we can provision a scoped key and enable prefix KV caching for their test data.

I'll drop a short table with numbers if Marissa wants to propose price points.

—Dev
